observedP10FailureSemantics.conclusion: P10 V2 never proved the dedicated Google Chrome test window was the Win32 foreground window before the attempted switch, and the foreground HWND did not change during the attempted helper activation. The prior native-blur PASS condition was therefore never reached.

documentHasFocus.meaning: DOM/browser-context focus predicate for the document
documentHasFocus.requiredRole: corroborating page-state check only after HWND/PID foreground identity is independently proven

hwnd.canProveNativeForeground: only when compared to GetForegroundWindow and mapped to the expected process identity

getForegroundWindowPid.meaning: GetForegroundWindow returns the current native foreground HWND; GetWindowThreadProcessId maps that HWND to an owning PID
getForegroundWindowPid.requiredRole: authoritative foreground-switch gate at the sampled instant
getForegroundWindowPid.warning: title or Chrome_WidgetWin_1 class alone is insufficient because Helium and Google Chrome are both Chromium-based

eventIsTrusted.meaning: browser reports the event as user-agent generated rather than script dispatchEvent
eventIsTrusted.requiredRole: supporting browser-event provenance only; CDP/browser automation may still yield trusted events

powerEventCount.meaning: DOM display of canonical session event count
powerEventCount.expectedSequence: baseline N; POWER keydown => N+1; blur cancellation => N+2 exactly; later keyup after cancellation => remains N+2
powerEventCount.requiredRole: detect duplicate/orphan/stray input edges in the bounded integration test
powerEventCount.warning: eventCount alone does not prove which Win32 window owned foreground; it must be combined with native HWND/PID and blur evidence

rootCauseInP10Harness: page.bring_to_front() activates the Playwright page/tab but was treated as if it established native Win32 foreground ownership; no HWND/PID ownership precondition was checked before keydown.

focus_start.document.hasFocus()==true was used as a proxy for 'Chrome actually in foreground'; V2 evidence demonstrates that this proxy was insufficient because the Win32 foreground remained the existing Helium window.

The helper activation path used Tk lift/focus_force, SetForegroundWindow and then cursor/mouse injection, but the harness did not first prove the test Chrome native HWND, nor did it require the helper HWND/PID to become GetForegroundWindow before reading DOM blur state.
The static eventProvenance text claimed a real Win32 foreground change before the foreground-change assertion had actually passed, permitting misleading receipt wording even on FAIL.

preferredMethod: Before launching a future dedicated test browser, snapshot all visible top-level HWND/PID/executable tuples.
Give the test page a unique QA-only window title token, e.g. FCV588-P11-QA-<run-id>, so the native browser top-level window can be found without relying on generic Chrome_WidgetWin_1 class alone.

Enumerate visible top-level windows with EnumWindows; for candidate title token use GetWindowThreadProcessId(hwnd) and verify the owning executable resolves to the exact intended Google Chrome binary, not Helium or another Chromium shell.
Require exactly one matching visible top-level HWND. If zero or multiple candidates remain after executable/path and unique-title filtering, return HARNESS_BLOCKED_AMBIGUOUS_CHROME_HWND.

Optionally bind the candidate PID to the dedicated browser process family using a unique QA profile/user-data-dir or a pre/post process snapshot. This is corroboration; HWND+PID+exact executable+unique title are the minimum native identity gates.

accept: P07/P09/runtime source hashes match their sealed authorities
QA port is closed before run; user-owned port4173 remains untouched
original user foreground HWND/PID/title are captured for cleanup only
test Chrome native HWND is uniquely identified and bound to expected Google Chrome executable/PID
helper native HWND is uniquely identified and bound to the harness/helper PID
gate0Preflight.failure: Any missing or ambiguous HWND/PID/executable binding => HARNESS_BLOCKED before POWER input

gate1EstablishTestChromeForeground.actionForFutureAuthorizedRun: request activation of the identified test-Chrome HWND, then bounded-poll GetForegroundWindow
accept: GetForegroundWindow() == testChromeHwnd
GetWindowThreadProcessId(testChromeHwnd).pid == bound test-Chrome top-level PID
foreground process executable is the expected Google Chrome binary
document.hasFocus() == true
document.activeElement is #key-power
gate1EstablishTestChromeForeground.failure: If native foreground cannot be established within bounded polling, return HARNESS_BLOCKED_CHROME_NOT_FOREGROUND; do not send POWER keydown

gate2EnterSinglePowerHold.inputClassification: Playwright page.keyboard.down is browser automation input; even if resulting DOM KeyboardEvent.isTrusted is true it must not be described as a physical human keyboard event
accept: eventCount baseline N recorded immediately before keydown
after one Space keydown, powerPressing == true
eventCount == N+1 exactly
test Chrome HWND remains GetForegroundWindow before initiating helper switch
gate2EnterSinglePowerHold.failure: Any duplicate count, missing pressing state or foreground drift => FAIL_INPUT_PRECONDITION

gate3ProveNativeForegroundSwitch.preferredAutomaticActionForFutureRun: Show/restore helper window if necessary, call SetForegroundWindow(helperHwnd), then bounded-poll GetForegroundWindow without moving the user's cursor or synthesizing a mouse click by default
accept: GetForegroundWindow() == helperHwnd
GetWindowThreadProcessId(helperHwnd).pid == helperPid
GetForegroundWindow() != testChromeHwnd
foreground PID is not the bound test-Chrome top-level PID
gate3ProveNativeForegroundSwitch.failure: If Windows foreground-lock rules reject SetForegroundWindow, return HARNESS_BLOCKED_FOREGROUND_SWITCH. Do not call this a product FAIL and do not force success with cursor movement, AttachThreadInput, settings changes or undocumented hacks.
gate3ProveNativeForegroundSwitch.portableManualFallback: In a separately authorized interactive run, an operator click on the already-visible QA helper window is the most portable way to satisfy Windows foreground policy; acceptance still depends on the same GetForegroundWindow/HWND/PID gates.

accept: only after Gate3 native switch passed: document.hasFocus() == false
at least one window blur event was recorded after keydown; isTrusted may be retained only as supporting metadata
powerPressing == false
eventCount == N+2 exactly, proving exactly one canonical post-down edge
status/power state remains equal to pre-hold baseline so the short/cancelled hold did not power-toggle the device

gate5ReleaseWithoutStrayEdge.actionForFutureAuthorizedRun: release the Playwright Space key while the page is still backgrounded, before restoring user foreground
accept: eventCount remains N+2 after keyup
powerPressing remains false
gate5ReleaseWithoutStrayEdge.failure: Any N+3 event or renewed pressing state => FAIL_STRAY_KEYUP_AFTER_CANCEL

safeRestoreOrder: close/destroy QA helper after keyup and final cancellation snapshot
if the original pre-test foreground HWND still exists, request SetForegroundWindow(originalForegroundHwnd) and bounded-poll for equality
if the original HWND is gone, do not guess another user window; record CLEANUP_ORIGINAL_WINDOW_GONE
if Windows denies restoration, record CLEANUP_FOREGROUND_RESTORE_BLOCKED and ask the operator to click their original window; do not move the cursor or inject clicks silently
close QA browser/server and verify QA port closed; verify user-owned 4173 owner/PID unchanged
gate6CleanupAndRestore.accept: Functional native-blur result may only be published together with a successful or explicitly acknowledged cleanup status; user foreground restoration failure must be visible in the receipt, never silently hidden.

mustRecord: test Chrome HWND/PID/title/executable and exact browser binary path
GetForegroundWindow snapshots before keydown, immediately before switch, after switch, and during cleanup restore
document.hasFocus, activeElement id, powerPressing, eventCount and status at baseline/down/blur/keyup stages
blur/focus event timestamps and isTrusted as supporting metadata
exact failure gate and error when any native transition cannot be proven
source/runtime hashes and port ownership before/after
receiptRequirementsForFutureRun.rule: Only set PASS_GENUINE_WIN32_BLUR_CANCELS_POWER_HOLD after all Gate0-Gate5 acceptance conditions pass in order; derive eventProvenance text from observed gates after the fact rather than hard-coding it before execution.

acceptanceRecommendation.nextRun: Use the fail-closed HWND/PID-identified sequence above in one authorized interactive/native run. If test Chrome cannot be made native foreground or helper cannot become foreground, stop as HARNESS_BLOCKED rather than modifying Windows settings or forcing focus with invasive workarounds.
